title: Matrix Multiplication Tensor Rank
tagline: Strassen multiplied 2x2 with 7 mults in 1969. For 5x5, the record is 96. Beat it.
description: Find a bilinear algorithm that multiplies an n x m matrix by an m x p matrix using fewer scalar multiplications than the current record. Equivalently, find a lower-rank decomposition of the matrix multiplication tensor T(n,m,p). Square and rectangular cases both count.
context: The naive method multiplies an n x m by an m x p matrix using nmp multiplications. Strassen (1969) showed 2x2 can be done in 7 instead of 8. For square matrices, records have improved slowly: R(3,3,3) <= 21 since 1976, R(5,5,5) <= 96 since 2022. Rectangular cases like R(2,3,4) and R(3,3,6) are less studied and may be more tractable. DeepMind's AlphaTensor (2022) found improvements over finite fields but matched or fell short over the integers. All submissions must work over standard arithmetic (integers/rationals).

leaderboard.note: Records over integers/rationals. Finite-field results (e.g. AlphaTensor over F2) excluded.

rows.note: Lower bound 49 — tight but optimality unproved

verification: Runs the algorithm on 100 random integer matrix pairs (n x m times m x p). Checks exact equality with A*B. All coefficients must be rational.

howToStart.title: Implement Strassen
howToStart.body: The 2x2 case with 7 multiplications. Understand how the 7 products reconstruct all 4 output entries — this is the template for all tensor-rank algorithms.

howToStart.title: Pick a target
howToStart.body: R(5,5,5) has the largest gap for square cases. Rectangular cases like R(3,3,6) and R(4,4,5) are less studied and may yield to fresh approaches.

howToStart.title: Tensor decomposition
howToStart.body: The multiplication tensor for (n,m,p) has shape nm x mp x np. Decompose into r rank-1 terms. Each term = one scalar multiplication.

howToStart.title: Search methods
howToStart.body: Gradient descent on decomposition error with random restarts. AlphaTensor used MCTS + RL. Simpler evolutionary approaches also work.

bounds.name: Best 23, lower bound 19
bounds.formula: Makarov & Laderman (1976). Gap open for 50 years.

bounds.name: Less studied
bounds.formula: Lower bounds weaker. R(2,3,4), R(3,3,6), R(4,4,5) all have room.

bounds.name: Exponent <= 2.371552
bounds.formula: Williams et al. (2024). Lower bound 2. Whether omega = 2 is open.
